title: Absorbed iron from one food, declared under FDP-1, evaluated for two host states
note: Same food and same declared inputs feed two scores that differ only in host iron status. Absorbed iron differs ~6x between a replete and a deficient host, yet BOTH scores carry provenance_grade '—': one required modifier (polyphenols) is OPEN, and by the weakest-link rule (FDP-1 §3.1) an OPEN input caps the whole score's provenance. That is the point of the example, not a bug to be fixed later by filling the gap — a confidently computed number whose provenance is honestly ungraded. Each nutrient_ref is a FOOD-COMPOSITION nutrient identifier (a USDA FDC nutrient number or an INFOODS tagname), NOT a metabolite id: FDP-1 declares layer-2 food composition, and mapping a nutrient onto a body metabolite (e.g. iron -> exchange metabolite fe2 / chebi:29033, via MASTER_CROSSWALK.tsv) is a separate downstream join. The identifiers here are illustrative; total polyphenols in particular has no single universally-standardized component tag, which is part of why it is the unmeasured (OPEN) input.

food.name: Black beans, cooked, boiled, without salt

validation.citation: Hallberg L, Hulthén L. Prediction of dietary iron absorption. Am J Clin Nutr. 2000;71(5):1147-1160. PMID:10799377
